# `silk/platform/windows/process`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Direct Windows child execution with explicit inherited handles and owned process cleanup.

## Details
Executable and working-directory paths use the machine namespace `/C:/...` or `/UNC/...`.
Arguments and environment values use canonical WTF-8. No shell or executable search runs.
Output pipes use overlapped reads so either stream can fill while the other is idle.

Import as `WindowsProcess` with `import silk.platform.windows.process { WindowsProcess }`.

<a id="WindowsProcess.impl.execute"></a>

### Associated function `execute`

```silk
pub effect fn execute(request: &ProcessRequest) -> ProcessOutcome ! ProcessError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Executes an absolute machine-path executable with the request's explicit arguments and environment.

#### Details

Paths use `/C:/...` or `/UNC/...`; text arguments are not path-converted. Raw values must be
canonical WTF-8. Case-insensitive duplicate environment names and `.bat`/`.cmd` programs are
refused before launch. The child receives EOF on stdin and only its three standard handles.
It starts suspended, enters a kill-on-close job, then runs without a console window. Both
output streams drain concurrently. When the child exits, remaining descendants are terminated.
All 32 exit bits are preserved as `i32`; an NTSTATUS-shaped value alone is not classified as a crash.

#### Errors

- `ProcessError` for invalid input or an OS spawn, wait, or capture failure.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if input or capture storage cannot be allocated.

#### Gotchas

Blocks the calling thread. Failure after launch terminates and waits for the owned process
and cancels pending reads before freeing their storage. A trap can bypass language cleanup;
the OS still closes the job when the parent process terminates.
